name: Essential Dignities & Rulerships — the traditional scheme, planet by planet and sign by sign
description: Essential dignities and rulerships as a LENS grammar: the seven classical planets, each carrying its domicile(s), exaltation (with the traditional degree), detriment, and fall — and the twelve signs, each stating its ruler, exaltation, detriment, and fall from the sign's side, so sign queries answer too. The scheme tabled here is the one Ptolemy and Lilly share. MATCHER KEYS: planet items carry category:'planet' + metadata.planet ('Sun'…'Saturn'); sign items carry category:'sign' + metadata.sign — the same convention grammars/western-astrology-canonical uses, so this grammar federates automatically into every 'every voice' stack (lenses, wheel, archetypal). Machine-readable dignity keys ride along in metadata: domicile[], exaltation, exaltation_degree, detriment[], fall on planet items; ruler, exaltation, exaltation_degree, detriment, fall (and modern_co_ruler where one exists) on sign items. PROVENANCE, honestly: the domicile/detriment scheme and the exaltation SIGNS are in Ptolemy (Tetrabiblos Book I — the houses of the planets, and the exaltations, with reasons but NO degrees) and in Lilly's table of essential dignities (Christian Astrology, 1647); the exaltation DEGREES are older than either English edition — the Dorotheus/al-Biruni lineage descending from Babylonian practice — and were cross-checked this session against multiple independent listings (Wikipedia's 'Exaltation (astrology)' article; al-Biruni's Book of Instruction and Dorotheus's Carmen Astrologicum as reported by secondary scholarship; renaissanceastrology.com's exaltation-degrees page): Sun 19° Aries, Moon 3° Taurus, Mercury 15° Virgo, Venus 27° Pisces (some sources give 28°), Mars 28° Capricorn, Jupiter 15° Cancer, Saturn 21° Libra — all sources consulted agree, with only the Venus 27°/28° variation noted. The strength-scoring point system quoted in the 'What dignity means' sections is Lilly's: domicile +5, exaltation +4, triplicity +3, term +2, face +1; detriment −5, fall −4; a planet with no essential dignity at all is 'peregrine.' Modern outer-planet co-rulerships (Uranus–Aquarius, Neptune–Pisces, Pluto–Scorpio) appear ONLY in the Canonical sections and are clearly marked as modern additions — they are not part of the traditional scheme. Triplicity, term, and face sub-rulers are NOT tabled here (they genuinely differ by tradition — Dorothean vs Ptolemaic triplicities, Egyptian vs Ptolemaic terms); contributors welcome to add them as their own clearly-sourced layer.

dating.label: Undated — contemporary lens compilation of the traditional dignities table. Its layers are dated in the item sections (Ptolemy c. 150 CE; Lilly 1647; public-domain enrichment from Raphael 1828 and Sepharial 1920); the table itself belongs to no single edition.

sections.Dignities table: Domicile: Leo · Exaltation: Aries (19°) · Detriment: Aquarius · Fall: Libra
sections.What dignity means: [William Lilly, Christian Astrology, 1647; general doctrine quoted via Zadkiel's 1852 abridgment] Essential dignity is placement-strength, and Lilly scores it: domicile +5, exaltation +4, triplicity +3, term +2, face +1; detriment −5, fall −4; a planet with no dignity at all is 'peregrine' — a wanderer. In its own house a planet "represents a man in such a condition as that he is lord of his own house, estate, and fortune"; exalted, "a person of haughty condition, arrogant, assuming more to himself than his due" — dignity is strength, not niceness. So the Sun in Leo commands from home ground; exalted at 19° Aries it blazes at its most assertive (and most self-important); in Aquarius (detriment) and Libra (fall) the royal claim is a guest in signs that answer to Saturn. (Scoring corroborated across multiple independent sources this session; the two quoted phrases rest on Zadkiel's public-domain abridgment of Lilly; confidence: medium.)
sections.Canonical: Modern astrology keeps the Sun's rulership of Leo unchanged — no discovered planet ever claimed it. The exaltation-in-Aries / fall-in-Libra axis is usually read psychologically now: identity most radiant where it initiates, most diffuse where it defers.
sections.The record — Raphael (A Manual of Astrol: [Raphael, A Manual of Astrology, 1828] “The Sun is considered as temperately hot and dry, of his own nature scarcely good or evil, but a most powerful source of ill fortune where afflicted by the other planets, and placed in his debilities, or signs contrary to his nature; as on the contrary, when strongly aspected or placed … in signs of dignity … he is the source of much prosperity.” Of the native “when principal significator”: “a large bony athletic strong body, broad high forehead, light sandy curling hair, quick piercing eye, and well made person … If well dignified or favourably aspected, the disposition is noble, magnanimous, proud and lofty, but humane; a faithful friend, and a generous enemy, scorning to use advantages which may be given him over his opponents … If ill dignified, and ill aspected, the native is both proud and mean, arrogant and submissive, a tyrant, and yet a sycophant, empty, vain, a great talker, restless, vain boasting, uncharitable, despotical, unfeeling.” (Verbatim from the 1828 djvu text this session, spelling as printed; confidence: high.)
sections.The record — Sepharial (Astrology: How t: [Sepharial, Astrology: How to Make and Read Your Own Horoscope, 1920] “The Sun renders its subjects magnanimous, noble, proud, despising all mean and sordid actions; loyal, truthful, and fearless. It produces honours and the favour of dignitaries, and renders the subject fortunate in the control of his affairs. In the body it controls the vital principle.” Nearly a century after Raphael, the same vocabulary of nobility and honour survives almost unchanged — worth noting as continuity, not claimed as this compiler's judgment. (Verbatim from the Project Gutenberg edition this session; confidence: high.)

sections.Dignities table: Domicile: Cancer · Exaltation: Taurus (3°) · Detriment: Capricorn · Fall: Scorpio
sections.What dignity means: [William Lilly, Christian Astrology, 1647] By Lilly's scoring (domicile +5, exaltation +4; detriment −5, fall −4, with triplicity, term, and face as the lesser dignities of +3/+2/+1) the Moon is strongest at home in Cancer, where her tides are her own, and exalted at 3° Taurus — the zodiac's most changeable body given its steadiest ground. In Capricorn (detriment) her nurture is rationed by rule; in Scorpio (fall) her instinct runs to extremes. (Placements: high confidence, heavily cross-corroborated; the reading is this compiler's gloss on the shared table, not Lilly's wording.)
sections.Canonical: Modern astrology keeps the Moon's rulership of Cancer unchanged. The exaltation at 3° Taurus is among the oldest attested of all the degrees — Dorotheus's Carmen already carries it — and is usually read now as feeling finding safety in the body and the ordinary.
sections.The record — Raphael (A Manual of Astrol: [Raphael, A Manual of Astrology, 1828] “The Moon, the companion of the earth, and chief source of our evening light, is a cold, moist, watery, phlegmatic planet, variable to an extreme … and partaking of good or evil, as she is aspected by good or evil stars. When angular and unafflicted in a nativity, she is the promissory pledge of great success in life, and continual good fortune … Her conjunction, semisextile, sextile, or trine, to Jupiter, is exceedingly fortunate.” Her enemies are given as Saturn and the Sun, her other aspects friendly. (Verbatim from the 1828 djvu text this session; confidence: high.)
sections.The record — Sepharial (Astrology: How t: [Sepharial, Astrology: How to Make and Read Your Own Horoscope, 1920] “The Moon gives gracefulness of manner and suavity of speech, softness and adaptability of nature, variableness, love of change, romance, and adventure; disposed to exploration and voyaging. In the body it corresponds to the glandular system, and its diseases are those incidental to the lymphatic glands and vascular tissue.” (Verbatim from the Project Gutenberg edition this session; confidence: high.)

sections.Dignities table: Domicile: Gemini, Virgo · Exaltation: Virgo (15°) · Detriment: Sagittarius, Pisces · Fall: Pisces
sections.What dignity means: [William Lilly, Christian Astrology, 1647] Mercury is the scheme's singular case: exalted in a sign he also rules — Lilly's own chapter calls Virgo "the house and exaltation of Mercury" (wording verified in this repo's grammars/william-lilly-christian-astrology) — so at 15° Virgo he can hold domicile and exaltation at once, +9 in Lilly's arithmetic, the strongest essential placement the table allows. The mirror is just as singular: in Pisces he is in detriment AND fall together, doubly debilitated. (Placements: high confidence; the Virgo quote is verified; the rest is gloss on the shared table.)
sections.Canonical: Modern astrology keeps Mercury's rulership of both Gemini and Virgo — no outer planet took either. The Virgo/Pisces axis is the tradition's cleanest teaching case: analysis exalted where it discriminates, undone where everything dissolves.
sections.The record — Raphael (A Manual of Astrol: [Raphael, A Manual of Astrology, 1828] “Mercury is the Astrological source of wit, ingenuity, invention, discovery, and eminent skill in science, art, and almost every important branch of human knowledge … when well dignified or free from hostile aspects of afflicting stars, the mind is strong, vigorous, active … the memory retentive, tenacious … generally the most eloquent orators, the most skilful philosophers, the most eminent mathematicians … are under his selectest influence … but when Mercury is afflicted or ill dignified by aspect, configuration, or discordancy of sign, the native will be a mean, shuffling, unprincipled character, a voucher of falsehoods, and void of real understanding.” (Verbatim from the 1828 djvu text this session; confidence: high.)
sections.The record — Sepharial (Astrology: How t: [Sepharial, Astrology: How to Make and Read Your Own Horoscope, 1920] “Mercury renders its subjects active, versatile, apt and business-like, disposed to much commerce, whether of the mind or the market, and eager in the pursuit of knowledge; alert, and well-informed. Its influence on affairs of life is variable, for it always translates the nature of that planet to which at birth it is in nearest aspect.” (Verbatim from the Project Gutenberg edition this session; confidence: high.)

sections.Dignities table: Domicile: Taurus, Libra · Exaltation: Pisces (27°) · Detriment: Scorpio, Aries · Fall: Virgo
sections.What dignity means: [William Lilly, Christian Astrology, 1647] By Lilly's scoring Venus rules from two homes — earthy Taurus and airy Libra — and is exalted at 27° Pisces (the one degree where the old tables genuinely waver: some sources give 28°), where sympathy is boundless. Lilly's own Pisces chapter states the placement — Pisces as "the house of Jupiter, and exaltation of Venus" (verified in grammars/william-lilly-christian-astrology). In Scorpio and Aries (detriment) her arts serve Mars's ends; in Virgo (fall) the tradition reads her as most out of place — affection under analysis. (Placements: high confidence; the 27°/28° variance is noted honestly.)
sections.Canonical: Modern astrology keeps Venus ruling Taurus and Libra. The exaltation in Pisces reads now as love universalized past the personal; the fall in Virgo as the old scheme's warning about perfecting what wants to be enjoyed.
sections.The record — Raphael (A Manual of Astrol: [Raphael, A Manual of Astrology, 1828] “She is a feminine, nocturnal, temperate planet, and considered as next to Jupiter in benevolent influence … If well dignified, well placed, or well aspected … the temper is even, quiet, placid, and unusually graceful; engaging, sweet, merry and cheerful; amateurs in music, drawing, and accomplishments … But if Venus be afflicted the native born under her immediate influence, is lewd, profligate, shameless, and lascivious … the real nature of Venus (Astrologically speaking) is mildness and goodness.” (Verbatim from the 1828 djvu text this session; confidence: high.)
sections.The record — Sepharial (Astrology: How t: [Sepharial, Astrology: How to Make and Read Your Own Horoscope, 1920] “Venus confers poesy, good taste, fine feeling, artistic powers, gentleness, docility, dalliance, and love of pleasure. It renders the affairs pleasant and prosperous, giving profit from both artistic and rustic pursuits. Next to Jupiter it is the most benefic of the planets in its action on mankind.” Sepharial ranks Venus “next to Jupiter” in benevolence — the identical ranking Raphael gives in 1828, an unbroken bit of manual-tradition doctrine. (Verbatim from the Project Gutenberg edition this session; confidence: high.)

sections.Dignities table: Domicile: Aries, Scorpio · Exaltation: Capricorn (28°) · Detriment: Libra, Taurus · Fall: Cancer
sections.What dignity means: [William Lilly, Christian Astrology, 1647] Mars rules day-Aries and night-Scorpio, and is exalted at 28° Capricorn — both Ptolemy and Lilly state the sign: "Capricorn is the house of Saturn and exaltation of Mars" (Ashmand, verified via grammars/tetrabiblos-ashmand), and Lilly's Capricorn chapter says the same (verified via grammars/william-lilly-christian-astrology). The old reading: choler disciplined into strategy — the soldier under command. In Libra and Taurus (detriment) the blade is a guest in Venus's houses; in Cancer (fall) heat drowns in moisture, force turned moody. (Placements: high confidence.)
sections.Canonical: Modern astrology keeps Mars ruling Aries, and after Pluto's discovery (1930) most modern astrologers give Scorpio to Pluto — a MODERN addition, with Mars retained as traditional or co-ruler. The exaltation in Capricorn still reads as aggression at its most effective: aimed, patient, structural.
sections.The record — Raphael (A Manual of Astrol: [Raphael, A Manual of Astrology, 1828] “He is a hot, dry, fiery, choleric, nocturnal, malignant, and violent planet, the Astrological cause of anger, quarrels, contention, violence, war, slaughter and bloodshed … when he is fortunate by aspect with the leading significators, and well dignified, he is said to produce a fearless, violent, irascible, and unsubmitting person, naturally delighting in war, battle, or contention, but in other respects prudent, rational, and even generous or magnanimous. If unfortunate in configurations and ill dignified, the native is wholly destitute of any virtue, prone to violence, quarrels, treachery, robbery, murder, treason, and every species of cruelty and wickedness.” (Verbatim from the 1828 djvu text this session; confidence: high.)
sections.The record — Sepharial (Astrology: How t: [Sepharial, Astrology: How to Make and Read Your Own Horoscope, 1920] “Mars confers a sense of freedom, much ambition and executive ability, frankness, truthfulness, and scorn of consequence. It renders the mind forceful and militant, stimulates to new projects and enterprises … Its diseases are those which arise from inflammatory action in the tissues.” (Verbatim from the Project Gutenberg edition this session; confidence: high.)

sections.Dignities table: Domicile: Sagittarius, Pisces · Exaltation: Cancer (15°) · Detriment: Gemini, Virgo · Fall: Capricorn
sections.What dignity means: [William Lilly, Christian Astrology, 1647] The greater benefic rules fiery Sagittarius by day and watery Pisces by night, and is exalted at 15° Cancer — generosity nourished, expansion given a home to grow in. By Lilly's scoring (+5 domicile, +4 exaltation) a well-placed Jupiter is the chart's most reliable fortune; in Gemini and Virgo (detriment) breadth is chopped into Mercury's particulars, and in Capricorn (fall) bounty is put on Saturn's budget. (Placements: high confidence, cross-corroborated; the reading is gloss on the shared table.)
sections.Canonical: Modern astrology keeps Jupiter ruling Sagittarius, and after Neptune's discovery (1846) most modern astrologers give Pisces to Neptune — a MODERN addition, with Jupiter retained as traditional or co-ruler. Exaltation in Cancer still reads as growth rooted in belonging.
sections.The record — Raphael (A Manual of Astrol: [Raphael, A Manual of Astrology, 1828] “He is found to be a planet in nature hot and moist, sanguine and diurnal, the author next under divine providence, of every earthly good … equally as powerful in good, as Saturn was before described to be in evil; the cause of riches, honors, and the greatest success in life. If Jupiter be fortified by dignities or aspects at birth, the native will be wise, just, good, affable, magnanimous, mild and temperate in manners … If ill dignified or ill fortified and afflicted … he will be a squanderer of his wealth, a prodigal, reckless of shame, of shallow abilities, easily led astray by fools … The real nature of Jupiter is freedom, confidence, generosity, frankness, benevolence, charity, good will, and nobleness of disposition, being the exact reverse of the mistrust and cunning of Saturn.” (Verbatim from the 1828 djvu text this session; confidence: high.)
sections.The record — Sepharial (Astrology: How t: [Sepharial, Astrology: How to Make and Read Your Own Horoscope, 1920] “Jupiter gives joviality, optimism, bountifulness, generosity, a rich and fruitful mind. It renders the subject fortunate in his affairs, giving success and frequently opulence. With this planet strong in the horoscope a person never ‘goes under.’” (Verbatim from the Project Gutenberg edition this session; confidence: high.)

sections.Dignities table: Domicile: Capricorn, Aquarius · Exaltation: Libra (21°) · Detriment: Cancer, Leo · Fall: Aries
sections.What dignity means: [William Lilly, Christian Astrology, 1647] Saturn rules the two signs opposite the luminaries' homes — Capricorn against the Moon's Cancer, Aquarius against the Sun's Leo (Ptolemy's own stated logic: the coldest, farthest planet given the signs farthest from the lights) — and is exalted at 21° Libra: the weigher exalted in the sign of the scales, severity refined into judgment. By Lilly's scoring a dignified Saturn is not warm but it is SOLID: the man who is "lord of his own house, estate, and fortune," however plainly he lives. In Cancer and Leo (detriment) his economy is a guest of the lights; in Aries (fall) deliberation is asked to sprint. (Placements: high confidence; al-Biruni and Dorotheus both carry the 21° Libra degree.)
sections.Canonical: Modern astrology keeps Saturn ruling Capricorn, and after Uranus's discovery (1781) most modern astrologers give Aquarius to Uranus — a MODERN addition, with Saturn retained as traditional or co-ruler. The exaltation in Libra survives intact in modern practice: limits at their best when they are fair.
sections.The record — Raphael (A Manual of Astrol: [Raphael, A Manual of Astrology, 1828] “Saturn is by universal experience acknowledged to be the most powerful, evil, and malignant of all the planets. In Nativities he is most destructive … If well dignified by house, exaltation, or aspect, the native will be acute, active, and penetrating; but austere, slow, and reserved, grave, close, and ungenerous, covetous, laborious, patient, and mindful of injuries; careful of what he gets, and constant both in attachment and hatred … If ill dignified, or ill aspected … the native will be sordid, base, cowardly and suspicious, envious, treacherous, malicious, and frowardly stubborn to a fault … In a word, Saturn is the greater infortune, the worst of all the planets.” (Verbatim from the 1828 djvu text this session; confidence: high.)
sections.The record — Sepharial (Astrology: How t: [Sepharial, Astrology: How to Make and Read Your Own Horoscope, 1920] “Saturn produces a thoughtful, sober, ponderable mind; steadfastness, patience, and endurance; disposition to routine and habit, method. In financial affairs it gives steady results commensurate with labour, success that is slow but sure, durance, hardships, privations.” Sepharial's Saturn keeps Raphael's “worst of all the planets” fatalism at a lower boil — privation rather than malignancy — which is the almanac tradition's own drift, not this compiler's softening of it. (Verbatim from the Project Gutenberg edition this session; confidence: high.)

sections.Dignities table: Ruler: Mercury · Exaltation: Mercury (15°) · Detriment: Jupiter · Fall: Venus
sections.Canonical: The scheme's singular sign: Lilly's own chapter calls Virgo "the house and exaltation of Mercury" (verified via grammars/william-lilly-christian-astrology) — the only place a classical planet rules AND is exalted at once. Mercury's rulership is unchanged in modern practice. Jupiter in detriment, Venus in fall: breadth and pleasure both submitted to analysis.
sections.The record — Raphael (A Manual of Astrol: [Raphael, A Manual of Astrology, 1828] “Virgo is the sixth sign … the house, exaltation and joy of Mercury; a cold, dry, earthy, feminine, nocturnal, melancholy, barren, humane, commanding sign. Those born solely under the rule of this sign, are of middle stature, but rarely handsome, slender, but very compact … very ingenious, thrifty, and economical.” (Verbatim from the 1828 djvu text this session; confidence: high.)

Under this sign, generally, the native is tall and well made, rather elegant in person, a round beautiful face … Authors state the disposition to be sweet, and the dealings and character just and upright.” (Verbatim from the 1828 djvu text this session; confidence: high.)

sections.Dignities table: Ruler: Mars · Exaltation: — (none in the classical seven-planet scheme) · Detriment: Venus · Fall: Moon
sections.Canonical: Mars's nocturnal house — Ptolemy: "Scorpio is, like Aries, the house of Mars, and also his joy" (verified via grammars/tetrabiblos-ashmand). MODERN ADDITION, clearly marked: after 1930 most modern astrologers assign Scorpio to Pluto, with Mars as traditional or co-ruler. Venus in detriment, the Moon in fall: affection and instinct both pulled into the sign's extremes.
sections.The record — Raphael (A Manual of Astrol: [Raphael, A Manual of Astrology, 1828] “Scorpio is the house of Mars, and also his joy. It is termed a cold, moist, watery, phlegmatic, feminine, nocturnal, fixed, mute, southern, and extremely fruitful sign … It produces a strong, corpulent, robust, bony person, dark curling hair and eyes … generally, they are very reserved in their mode of speech … It is a very peculiar sign for deceit, fraud, and hypocrisy.” (Verbatim from the 1828 djvu text this session; confidence: high.)

sections.Dignities table: Ruler: Saturn · Exaltation: Mars (28°) · Detriment: Moon · Fall: Jupiter
sections.Canonical: Saturn's nocturnal house — stated by both source voices: Ptolemy, "Capricorn is the house of Saturn and exaltation of Mars" (verified via grammars/tetrabiblos-ashmand), and Lilly's Capricorn chapter likewise (verified via grammars/william-lilly-christian-astrology). Rulership unchanged in modern practice. Mars exalted at 28°: aggression at its most effective — aimed, patient, structural. The Moon in detriment, Jupiter in fall: feeling and bounty both put on a budget.
sections.The record — Raphael (A Manual of Astrol: [Raphael, A Manual of Astrology, 1828] “Capricorn is a cold, earthy, melancholy, arid, nocturnal, southern … sign, the sign of the Winter tropic; the house of Saturn, and exaltation of Mars. It is accounted barren: it produces a dry constitution, slender make, with a long thin visage, thin beard, dark hair, long neck, narrow chin and breast, and weak knees. In disposition crafty, thrifty, subtle, and saving, witty, but changeable.” (Verbatim from the 1828 djvu text this session; confidence: high.)

sections.Dignities table: Ruler: Jupiter · Exaltation: Venus (27°) · Detriment: Mercury · Fall: Mercury
sections.Canonical: Jupiter's nocturnal house — stated by both source voices: Ptolemy, "Pisces is the house of Jupiter and exaltation of Venus" (verified via grammars/tetrabiblos-ashmand), and Lilly, "the house of Jupiter, and exaltation of Venus" (verified via grammars/william-lilly-christian-astrology). MODERN ADDITION, clearly marked: after 1846 most modern astrologers assign Pisces to Neptune, with Jupiter as traditional or co-ruler. Mercury is BOTH in detriment and in fall here — the table's sharpest debility, analysis dissolved. Venus exalted at 27° (some tables 28°): love universalized past the personal.
sections.The record — Raphael (A Manual of Astrol: [Raphael, A Manual of Astrology, 1828] “Pisces, the house of Jupiter, and exaltation of Venus, is a moist, cold, watery, phlegmatic, nocturnal, bicorporeal, effeminate, sickly, southern, obeying sign; producing a short, pale, fleshy person, stooping, thickset, round shouldered, and brown hair … It is exceedingly fruitful, and luxuriantly productive.” (Verbatim from the 1828 djvu text this session; confidence: high.)
